    1  """Plain-PyTorch reference for the TVD loss described in task.md.
    2  
    3  Same signature and output structure as entry.kernel(). Its float64 autograd is the trusted oracle.
    4  """
    5  import torch
    6  
    7  _REDUCTIONS = ("none", "sum", "mean", "batchmean")
    8  
    9  
   10  def reference(p, q, shift_labels=None, reduction="batchmean", ignore_index=-100):
   11      if reduction not in _REDUCTIONS:
   12          raise ValueError(f"reduction must be one of {_REDUCTIONS}, got {reduction!r}")
   13      BT, V = p.shape
   14      q = q.detach()  # constant target: no gradient flows to q
   15  
   16      tvd = 0.5 * torch.abs(p - q)  # (BT, V)
   17  
   18      if shift_labels is None:
   19          n_rows = BT
   20      else:
   21          keep = shift_labels != ignore_index  # (BT,)
   22          tvd = torch.where(keep.unsqueeze(1), tvd, torch.zeros_like(tvd))
   23          n_rows = int(keep.sum().item())
   24  
   25      if reduction == "none":
   26          return tvd
   27      total = tvd.sum()
   28      if reduction == "sum":
   29          return total
   30      if n_rows == 0:
   31          raise ValueError(f"reduction={reduction!r} needs at least one row whose label is not ignore_index")
   32      if reduction == "mean":
   33          return total / (n_rows * V)
   34      return total / n_rows  # batchmean

arguments.evidence: The kernel computes the gradient as tl.where(p > q, 0.5*scale, -0.5*scale) (tvd.py:89). At p == q this gives -0.5*scale. The float64 autograd of 0.5*|p-q| in reference.py uses sign(0) = 0, so the oracle gradient is 0 there. Any kept row with p[i,j] == q[i,j] therefore gets a wrong p.grad of -0.5*scale instead of 0. verdict.evidence: The kernel computes the gradient as tl.where(p > q, 0.5*scale, -0.5*scale) (tvd.py:89). At p == q this gives -0.5*scale. The float64 autograd of 0.5*|p-q| in reference.py uses sign(0) = 0, so the oracle gradient is 0 there. Any kept row with p[i,j] == q[i,j] therefore gets a wrong p.grad of -0.5*scale instead of 0. Using p = q makes every element tie, so the whole gradient is wrong. The loss, the scaling, the row masking and the reductions all look correct. I read the source only and did not run anything.
